shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat stone surface
winged creature / wing rendered with rows of parallel feathers
animals or creature bodies in profile
horizontal register band across the upper part
justification: Both surfaces show low-relief profile creatures with feather-like parallel striations and an upper horizontal register, and both include a bird-headed form, but A depicts a single large anthropomorphic winged figure with human head, beard, elaborate hair and raised arm dominating the whole panel, while B stacks several small schematic animals (bird, quadruped, snake-like forms) beneath a row of repeated hooked/hut-like signs and a fringed band. The relationships differ entirely: A is a unified single-figure composition with human anatomy and drapery detail, whereas B is an accumulation of separate zoomorphic and abstract signs in registers, so the correspondence is only at the generic level of relief animals and feather hatching.
